title: TDE self-UI proving experiment
objective: Test whether TDE can take a bounded product vision for a UI about TDE itself, convert that vision into canonical work, drive implementation through the real task/runtime path, and leave behind inspectable operated proof with limited manual rescue.

recommendedSlice.name: TDE Operator Readiness View
minimumContents: canonical tasks generated for the slice

preconditions: one explicit entry artifact remains canonical
bounded GO/NO-GO posture for DB/readiness is stated
successCriteria: bounded UI vision becomes explicit canonical work
work moves through the actual producer/adapter/runtime path
a working UI slice exists and reflects real state changes
at least one real post-build run/update/event is evidenced
a reviewer can inspect what happened without tribal knowledge
failureSignals: progress depends on undocumented manual stitching
the UI is manually populated rather than driven from real state
operation is not evidenced after implementation
evidence exists only as narrative reconstruction
nextAction: Perform one explicit runtime-closure hardening step, then instantiate the live experiment task set and evidence chain.
notes: This is intentionally a proving experiment, not a commitment to a full TDE UI program.
The experiment should attack the current bottleneck of inspectable runtime closure rather than optimizing for UI breadth or polish.
